title: Find Sorted Submatrices With Maximum Element at Most K
summary: Given a 2D matrix grid and a non-negative integer k, count the submatrices where the maximum element is at most k, and each row is sorted in non-increasing order.
statement: Given a 2D matrix grid and a non-negative integer k, count the submatrices where the maximum element is at most k, and each row is sorted in non-increasing order.
constraints: grid has 1–1,000 rows and columns with positive values; k is positive.
Count rectangular submatrices whose maximum is at most k and whose values in every selected row are non-increasing left to right.
Single-cell submatrices satisfy the ordering condition when their value is at most k.
hints: For each right column, every row has a maximum valid width ending there.
A rectangle’s valid left choices equal the minimum width across its selected row interval.
Update row widths from the bound and non-increasing rule, then sum all contiguous-row subarray minima with a monotonic stack.
Each rectangle is counted at its unique right edge, and its limiting row width gives exactly its allowed left edges.
editorial: Each rectangle is counted at its unique right edge, and its limiting row width gives exactly its allowed left edges.

tests.explanation: Eight rectangles lie entirely in bounded row segments that never increase to the right.
Every one of the 36 rectangular submatrices is bounded and row-wise non-increasing.
